prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Animula, vagula, blandula. Life! I know not what thou art, But know that thou and I must part; And when, or how, or where we met, I own to me’s a secret yet. But this I know, when thou art fled, Where’er they lay these limbs, this head, No clod so valueless shall be, As all that then remains of me. O whither, whither dost thou fly, Where bend unseen thy trackless course, And in this strange divorce, Ah tell where I must seek this compound I? To the vast ocean of empyreal flame, From whence thy essence came, Dost thou thy flight pursue, when freed From matter’s base encumbering weed? Or dost thou, hid from sight, Wait, like some spell-bound knight, Through blank oblivious years th’ appointed hour, To break thy trance and reassume thy power? Yet canst thou without thought or feeling be? O say what art thou, when no more thou ’rt thee? Life! we’ve been long together, Through pleasant and through cloudy weather; ’Tis hard to part when friends are dear; Perhaps ’t will cost a sigh, a tear; Then steal away, give little warning, Choose thine own time; Say not Good night, but in some brighter clime Bid me Good morning.

Here are two ways to polish this text, depending on your preferred format. 

### Option 1: Elevated & Eloquent Prose (Recommended for essays, speeches, or formal context)

> **Animula, vagula, blandula.**  
> 
> Little, fleeting, gentle soul. Life, though your true essence remains a mystery to me, I know with certainty that we must eventually part. How, when, or where our union began remains a secret hidden from my understanding. Yet this much I know: once you have departed, whatever earth receives these limbs and this head, no common clod of soil shall be less valuable than all that remains of me. 
> 
> Where do you vanish to? Along what invisible, trackless path do you journey in this strange separation? Tell me, where must I seek the unified self we created together? Do you fly back to that vast ocean of heavenly light from which your spirit first emerged, once released from the burdensome weight of mortal matter? Or do you lie hidden from sight, like an enchanted knight waiting through silent, forgotten years for the appointed hour to break your trance and reclaim your power? Yet can you truly exist without thought or sensation? What do you become when you are no longer yourself? 
> 
> Life, we have walked together for so long, through both fair weather and dark clouds. Parting is always difficult between dear companions, and it may well draw a sigh and a tear. Therefore, slip away quietly with little warning, and choose your own time. Do not bid me "Good night," but rather, in some brighter realm, greet me with "Good morning."

outputs.L2:
Here is a complete paraphrase of the text, maintaining all original details and ideas through restructured sentences and distinct phrasing:

O restless, gentle spirit. 

While the true nature of life remains an enigma to me, I am certain of one thing: we must eventually separate. I admit I still do not understand how, where, or under what circumstances our partnership first began. I do know with absolute certainty, however, that once you depart, my physical body—my head and limbs—will be laid to rest somewhere, and what remains of me will hold less value than the cheapest lump of dirt. 

Where are you rushing off to? What invisible, pathless route are you taking? In the course of this peculiar separation, tell me: where am I supposed to look for the unified self that we once formed together? 

Once you are liberated from the heavy, burdensome shell of physical matter, will you fly back to the immense sea of divine fire from which your spirit originally sprang? Or will you conceal yourself, like an enchanted knight in a trance, passing unremembered years in total darkness until the designated moment arrives for you to awaken and reclaim your power? Yet, can you truly exist without any thought or sensation? Please reveal what you actually become when you are no longer the entity you once were. 

Life, we have shared a lengthy journey together through both fair skies and stormy weather. Saying goodbye is painful when two companions care deeply for one another, and parting may well provoke a sigh or a tear. Therefore, slip away quietly without giving much advance notice; select your own moment to depart. Do not bid me farewell with a "Good night," but instead, welcome me with a "Good morning" in a far brighter world.
outputs.L3:
Though we may never fully comprehend the spark that first ignited human existence, one truth remains absolute: the quiet inevitability of our eventual departure. How life begins is shrouded in an enduring mystery, a secret held closely by the universe. Yet, regardless of how fiercely we cling to this world or how grand our earthly achievements may be, the moment of death awaits us all—an unavoidable threshold that every living creature must cross.

When that final hour arrives and life withdraws from the physical frame, a striking transformation takes place. The flesh, once vibrant and animated by thought, warmth, and emotion, is instantly stripped of its significance. Without the animating spirit within, the physical body becomes nothing more than a hollow vessel—an empty shell that has lost all its intrinsic value, rendered still and powerless.

This sudden vacancy naturally compels us to look beyond the physical world and ponder the fate of the unseen self. Where does the soul travel once it leaves the body? Does it ascend immediately, returning to the divine source from which it originated, merging back into a sacred cosmic whole? Or does it enter a quiet, dreamless slumber, resting patiently in the shadows until some appointed time of awakening? The true destination remains hidden behind the veil of eternity.

Reflecting on the passage of time, one cannot help but view life not merely as a biological state, but as a faithful companion. Together, we have walked a long and winding road, sharing moments of radiant joy as well as burdens of bitter grief. Through every season of light and hardship, this constant presence has sustained us, evolving into a deeply cherished friend whose companionship has defined our journey.

Because this bond has been so profound, the heart asks for only one final favor. When the hour of parting ultimately arrives, let there be no tragic, agonizing farewell. Instead, let life steal away gently and peacefully, slipping quietly into the night. We bid it adieu not with despair, but with the quiet hope that this goodbye is merely a temporary silence—and that one day, in a brighter and more luminous realm, we will greet each other once again.
outputs.L4:
Life, my oldest and most intimate companion, we have walked this long and winding road together since my very first breath. You have been the silent witness to every heartbeat, the invisible current animating my frame, and the faithful partner in every joy, grief, and quiet turn of my existence. Yet, despite a lifetime spent in your constant embrace, I find myself standing at the edge of thought, looking at you with a profound and reverent wonder. Who are you, really? And what am I, this temporary vessel you have chosen to inhabit?

When I look back into the morning mist of my beginnings, I search in vain for the moment our partnership started. My soul’s origin remains shrouded in absolute mystery, an unremembered dawn. Was I summoned from the vast, patient silence of the cosmos, or pulled from some eternal well of consciousness just to walk beside you for a brief hour under the sun? I do not know. I only know that I arrived, pulled into this earthly dance, bound to your restless and beautiful energy.

Now, as the twilight of this journey approaches and the physical vessel begins to tire, the deepest of all questions presses upon my heart: what becomes of this consciousness when our long walk ends? Where will the spark go when the lamp is extinguished? The mind reels at the threshold of physical death, grasping at the unknown destination that awaits when you and I must finally untangle our fingers. 

Yet, I feel no anger toward the inevitable end, nor do I view our eventual separation as a tragedy. Instead, I write this as a gentle petition to you, my dear friend. When the moment arrives for us to part, let it not be a scene of terror or violent struggle. I ask for no mournful lamentations, no desperate tearing at the edges of twilight, and no bitter resistance against the natural tide. 

Let our parting be as quiet and graceful as a late autumn leaf slipping from the branch to rest upon the earth. Let us slip away softly, with the quiet dignity of two travelers who have shared a rich, full day and now seek well-earned rest. 

For I have come to see that death is not the cruel thief we so often fear it to be, nor is it a dark and empty abyss. It is merely a threshold—a quiet transition from one state of being to another. You have taught me how to live, and in doing so, you have prepared me to let go. Death is simply your final gift: the peaceful closing of an earthly eye so that a deeper, grander vision might open. 

So let us finish this journey with grace, my beloved companion. When the dusk falls completely, do not grant me a fearful end, but a serene farewell. Bid me a gentle "goodnight" here in the shadows of this world, so that I may step across the threshold, unburdened and at peace, to wake to a brighter, eternal morning.
outputs.L5:
The ancient poets spoke of the *animula*—the “little soul,” a delicate flicker of consciousness arriving naked and quiet into the vastness of the universe. At the beginning, this small spirit is nothing more than potential: a soft breath wrapped in skin, untroubled by time, grief, or ambition. It exists in pure simplicity, asking only to be.

Then comes **life**. 

Life arrives not as a gentle stream, but as a rushing tide of sensory wonder and sudden storms. The animula learns the weight of gravity, the taste of salt and honey, the ache of longing, and the dizzying joy of love. It builds a sanctuary of memories, gathering names, places, and years like polished stones. It wears the heavy armor of identity, learning to navigate a world made of concrete and noise. 

**But** the spirit is never entirely at home in the solid world. 

As the years accumulate, the animula begins to feel the friction of existence. It discovers that to love is to risk loss, and to grow is to leave things behind. The world attempts to turn the little soul into something heavy, burdening it with regrets and unanswered questions. **But** beneath the scars and the exhaustion, the animula retains its original, quiet spark. It remains the curious wanderer, uncontained by the body it inhabits.

In the final reckoning, when the clamor of the world fades into silence, life is revealed for what it truly was: a vibrant, fleeting guest house. The mortal frame may yield, **but** the animula simply unspools itself from the earth, slipping back into the dark starlight—gentle, unburdened, and free once more.

counterfactuals.prompt: Combine the opening line of Emperor Hadrian's address to his soul ("Animula, vagula, blandula") with Anna Laetitia Barbauld's poem "Life" to create a single, continuous meditation on mortality.
counterfactuals.output:
*Animula, vagula, blandula,*  
Little wandering, tender soul,  
Guest and companion of the clay,  
Whither art thou bound away?  
Life! I know not what thou art,  
But know that thou and I must part;  
And when, or how, or where we met  
I own to me’s a secret yet.  

We’ve been long together,  
Through pleasant and through cloudy weather;  
’Tis hard to part when friends are dear—  
Perhaps ’twill cost a sigh, a tear;  
Now pale, and stiff, and naked left,  
Of all thy accustomed joys bereft,  
Into what dark and silent clime  
Dost thou drift beyond the reach of time?  

Yet mourn not the fading of the light,  
Nor fear the cold, approaching night.  
Steal away, give little warning,  
Choose thine own time;  
Say not *Good Night*,—but in some brighter clime  
Bid me *Good Morning*.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a classic 18th-century style poem about a dying person bidding a gentle, reflective farewell to life and the soul.
counterfactuals.output:
**A Valediction at Twilight: To the Body and the Soul**

The evening shades now softly round me close,
And mortal day surrenders to the night;
My weary eyes incline to sweet repose,
As fades the world’s diminishing delight.

Farewell, ye fields where youthful footsteps roved,
Ye fleeting joys, and sorrows long suppressed;
Farewell to all that mortal passion loved—
The fevered heart now whispers into rest.

And thou, my Soul, companion of my clay,
Soft guest that lodged within this fragile breast,
Prepare to wing thy unencumbered way
To realms where purer spirits find their rest.

No more shall Time his anxious reckonings keep,
Nor false Ambition mock my failing breath;
I stand upon the margins of the deep,
And greet with tranquil eyes the shade of Death.

He comes not clad in terrors to destroy,
Nor breaks this quiet hour with sudden strife;
He opens wide the gate to lasting joy,
And gently closes the brief dream of life.

Then fall, frail dust, into thy native earth,
While the freed spirit breaks its mortal bond,
To claim at last its high, celestial birth,
And wake serene in brighter realms beyond.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.output:
The mortal vessel yieldeth to the night,
The silver cord is snapped, the breath is spent;
My spirit riseth in a pale, soft light,
Unbound from clay, its earthly tenure rent.

Ah, wand'ring soul! Now whither dost thou hie?
Into what boundless ether art thou tossed?
Beyond the vaulted arches of the sky,
Art thou in shadow or in glory lost?

Where’er thy phantom footsteps now may stray,
Past suns forgotten and through realms unknown,
Doth memory linger on the vanished day,
Or must thou drift forevermore alone?

I cast a backward gaze upon the clay,
And all the world of light I leave behind—
The blooming rose, the break of golden day,
The sweet embraces of my mortal kind.

Sweet Life, farewell! Thy joy was laced with tears,
Yet fair thou wert, e'en in thy briefest sigh;
I step beyond the shadow of my years,
And bid thy gentle dust a fond goodbye.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a poetic text on death featuring Hadrian's "Animula vagula blandula" as an opener, followed by classic English romantic stanzas exploring the soul's journey and ending with "Bid me Good morning."
counterfactuals.output:
*Animula vagula blandula,*  
*Hospes comesque corporis,*  
*Quo nunc abibis in loca*  
*Pallidula, rigida, nudula,*  
*Nec, ut soles, dabis iocos?*  

***

Ah, little wandering soul, so frail and sweet,  
Once gentle guest within this house of clay,  
Where turn your naked, unremembered feet  
As evening steals the lingering light away?  
No longer shall your tender jests beguile,  
Nor laughter echo through the quiet hall;  
The shadow lengthens on the fading dial,  
And silence descends to claim the end of all.  

Yet do not dread the pale, unpathwayed dark,  
Nor shrink before the cold, mysterious sea;  
For like a rising, silver-throated lark,  
The spirit leaps, untrammeled, wild, and free.  
The heavy garments of the flesh are cast  
Into the quiet dust from whence they came;  
The weary heart finds resting place at last,  
Unbound from grief, from sorrow, and from name.  

Across the void where quiet starlight weaves  
A luminous path through realms unknown and vast,  
The soul ascends above the autumn leaves,  
Beyond the reaching shadows of the past.  
No phantom chill can touch the awakening mind,  
Nor linger in the breath of mortal sighs,  
For all the burdens that were left behind  
Dissolve like mist beneath unclouded skies.  

So speak no grief, nor murmur of "Good night,"  
When down the west the fading sun descends;  
For death is but the turning toward the light,  
The secret place where every journey ends.  
And when I step upon that further shore,  
Where endless day breaks glorious and bright,  
Look up above the shadows of before,  
And in that fairer land beyond the night,  

Bid me Good morning.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.output:
The dusk settles softly upon the windowpane,
A silent absolution for the sunshine and the rain.
The long day is over, the work is all complete,
And quiet shadows gather where the earth and heavens meet.

I loosen my grip on the threads of the day,
The memories fading like mist on the bay.
The laughter, the sorrow, the warmth of the sun,
Are folded like garments whose keeping is done.

My breath grows as light as a leaf on the air,
Unbound from the heavy routine and the care.
No fear in the darkness, no grief in the slow
Deep pull of the river that beckons me go.

So weep not for me as I step through the door;
I am not diminished, just weary no more.
I leave you my love in the quiet and still—
A shade in the meadow, a breeze on the hill.

A final soft whisper, the curtain is drawn,
I part from the twilight to search for the dawn.
